master.title: News reports in Russia: State prosecutor accuses jailed opposition figure Navalny of stealing 2.7 mln rubles from donors
master.content:
State prosecutor accuses jailed opposition figure Navalny of stealing 2.7 mln rubles from donors

POKROV (Vladimir region). Feb 15 (Interfax) - According to the state prosecution, jailed opposition figure Alexei Navalny has stolen nearly 2.7 million rubles donated to him, in particular, for the 2018 Russian presidential campaign, an Interfax correspondent reported from a court session.

According to the indictment read out by a prosecutor at Moscow's Lefortovsky District Court on Tuesday, Navalny is charged with four counts of especially largescale fraud and contempt of court.

According to the indictment, Navalny set up an organized group consisting of his associates Leonid Volkov, Roman Rubanov and other accomplices, who collected money from an undefined number of people for the activities of the Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK, designated as extremist and banned in Russia), the Foundation for Protection of Citizens' Rights (FZPG, designated as extremist and banned in Russia) and the Navalny Headquarters (designated as extremist and banned in Russia), as well as for Navalny's 2018 presidential campaign.

The prosecutor emphasized that Navalny collected campaign funds while he was convicted and deprived of his passive suffrage, thus misleading donors about his true goals.

The state prosecutor noted that the criminal group set up by Navalny was characterized by stability, clear distribution of roles and a common understanding of the criminal intent.

"The activities of the members of the organized group were distinguished by the consistency of methods and ways of criminal activity," the state prosecutor said.

The investigators established that Navalny and his accomplices have stolen and at their own discretion disposed of four citizens' funds to the total amount of 2,693,503 rubles.

Earlier, the Investigative Committee said that Navalny and his accomplices have used for their own purposes more than 356 million rubles out of the 588 million rubles donated to non-profit organizations headed by the opposition figure, but according to the indictment, the present case deals only with the fraud of 2.7 million rubles.

Moreover, according to the indictment, Navalny disregarded generally accepted rules of morals and decency, and seeking to humiliate her and obstruct proper legal proceedings, insulted Justice of the Peace Vera Akimova, who was trying a case against him for insulting Great Patriotic War veteran Ignat Artemenko in 2021.

The indictment contains, in particular, such statements by Navalny to Akimova: "Are you a gramophone or a judge?"; "If you interrupt me, I will remove you from the courtroom"; "Constantly talking like a parrot"; "Let me address you not as your honor, but as Obersturmbannfuhrer" and so on.

The investigators established that Navalny also insulted prosecutor Yekaterina Frolova, who supported the charges against him in the case of slander against a war veteran, and the grandson of this veteran, Igor Kolesnikov.

In turn, Navalny said that he did not admit the charges.

According to the opposition figure, what he is charged with is normal political activity.

"We have the most honest and transparent organization. And my evidence is the materials of the criminal case, which we will analyze. [...] We will expose this lie point by point," Navalny said, speaking in court.

He said he has been grateful to those who donated to his activities.

Moscow's Lefortovsky District Court on Tuesday began hearing Navalny's new case in an off-site session at Penal Colony No. 2 in the town of Pokrov in the Vladimir region.

Navalny has previously been put on trial several times, in particular, for embezzlement, business fraud, money laundering, and slander.

In 2021, Navalny was also identified as a defendant in criminal cases for setting up an extremist group and establishing an organization that encroached on the personality and rights of citizens.

The opposition figure is currently serving a three-and-a-half-year prison sentence imposed on him by Moscow's Zamoskvoretsky District Court in 2014 as part of the so-called Yves Rocher case.

In early 2021, immediately after Navalny returned from Germany, where he was being treated after an alleged poisoning, his initially suspended sentence in the Yves Rocher case was changed to real jail time at the Russian Federal Penitentiary Service's request due to his repeated violations of the restrictions and obligations imposed on him.
